newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends weaker as election fears grow.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends weaker as election fears grow.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar fell through 69 US cents at the close on Wednesday as fears of a National Party government defeat in Saturday's election pervaded the market, dealers said.
They said rumours that a TV3 political poll out tonight would show a dramatic decline in support for the conservative National Party had prompted investors to sell the Kiwi.
"The rumour is that National is going to come in a lot lower -- around 31 percent -- significantly lower than the market's expectations, and that's spooked a few people," a dealer said.
The Kiwi ended at US$0.6890/97 and at 65.83 on its Trade-Weighted Index, down from 0.6910/17 and 66.01 at the open.
"It's closing pretty offered, we've taken a lot of stop losses around the 0.6895/00 level on the close from New York and European names," said a dealer.
"We've basically seen investment banks selling all day, also Aussie hasn't performed and that's dragged Kiwi down a little bit as well."
Continued Eurokiwi and samurai issuance had tempered the Kiwi's weakness, but early corporate interest to buy had been overshadowed by profit-takers, leaving the currency vulnerable on the close.
Dealers said the market would get progressively more nervous as election day approached and all eyes would be on tonight's poll result at 6 p.m. (0500 GMT).
Dealers saw the Kiwi trading a 0.6875-6910 range overnight.
